title: Arabidopsis Leaf Protoplasting Protocol
author: Diep R R Ganguly
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.p9adr2e
materials: Use haemocytometer to calculate the concentration of protoplasts.

steps.title: Prepare Enzyme Solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 20 mM MES (pH 5.7), 0.4 M mannitol and 20 mM KCl in water, heat to 70 °C for 3–5 min, then add cellulose R10 (1.5 %) and macerozyme R10 (0.4 %). Warm the mixture to 55 °C for 10 min, cool to room temperature, and add 10 mM CaCl₂, 1–5 mM β‑mercaptoethanol (optional) and 0.1 % BSA. Filter through a 0.45 µm syringe filter into a petri dish; use fresh or store at 4 °C overnight.

steps.title: Prepare W5 and MMG Buffers
steps.instruction: Make W5 solution containing 2 mM MES (pH 5.7), 154 mM NaCl, 125 mM CaCl₂ and 5 mM KCl. Make MMG solution containing 4 mM MES (pH 5.7), 0.4 M mannitol and 15 mM MgCl₂.

steps.title: Prepare Plant Material
steps.instruction: Grow Arabidopsis plants 3–4 weeks old (pre‑flowering) and keep them in the dark overnight to deplete starch. Select well‑expanded leaves #5 and #7; about 40 leaves per 50 mL enzyme solution yield ~1.5 × 10⁶ protoplasts (≈3 µg RNA by TRIzol). For larger scale, use 100–150 leaves in 40–60 mL enzyme solution to obtain ~10⁷ protoplasts.

steps.title: Cut Leaf Strips
steps.instruction: Using a fresh, sharp razor blade on a clean surface, cut leaf tissue into 0.5–1 mm strips, gliding the blade to avoid crushing the tissue.

steps.title: Incubate Strips in Enzyme Solution
steps.instruction: Transfer the leaf strips quickly and gently into the enzyme solution, ensuring they are fully submerged.

steps.title: Digest in Dark
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube without shaking in the dark at room temperature for at least 3 hours; the solution should change from light brown to green after gentle swirling, indicating protoplast release.

steps.title: Check Protoplast Release
steps.instruction: Gently swirl the tube and examine under a microscope; Arabidopsis mesophyll protoplasts appear as 30–50 µm spherical cells.

steps.title: Dilute with W5 Solution
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of freshly prepared W5 solution to the enzyme/protoplast suspension.

steps.title: Filter Through Miracloth
steps.instruction: Rinse two clean layers of Miracloth in W5 solution, then filter the diluted suspension through the Miracloth layers into a clean container.

steps.title: Centrifuge Protoplasts
steps.instruction: Transfer the flow‑through to a 30 mL round‑bottom glass centrifuge tube and centrifuge at 150 g (rcf) for 2 minutes with the brake ON (hard stop). Remove as much supernatant as possible and gently swirl to resuspend the pellet.

steps.title: Resuspend in W5 to Desired Density
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in W5 solution to a final concentration of 2 × 10⁵ protoplasts / mL.

steps.title: Rest and Transfer to MMG
steps.instruction: Place the suspension on ice for at least 30 minutes to allow protoplasts to settle by gravity. Carefully remove most of the W5 without disturbing the pellet, then resuspend the cells at 2 × 10⁵ / mL in MMG solution kept at room temperature (count cells with a haemocytometer before this final resuspension).
